topic: Will the world's population keep growing indefinitely?
research_question: Under which joint fertility, mortality, migration, and climate-disruption trajectories does a calibrated cohort-component ensemble assign positive global population growth through 2100?
central_hypothesis: A jointly calibrated probabilistic cohort-component ensemble can distinguish post-2100 growth-persistence conditions from earlier-peak conditions; climate-disruption covariates deserve retention only if they improve held-out prediction and calibration beyond demographic components alone.

mechanism.state_update: For each country, age, sex, and year, the next cohort equals survivors from the previous cohort plus net migration; the youngest cohort is generated from age-specific fertility.
mechanism.aggregation: Country-age-sex posterior trajectories are summed to regional and global totals before calculating annual growth and first peak year.
mechanism.climate_boundary: Climate-disruption features are candidate lagged predictors in component models. They are not interpreted as universal causal effects without separate identification evidence.

alternative_explanations: Starting age structure and fertility convergence alone explain peak persistence, making climate features unnecessary.
Apparent climate value reflects correlated development, conflict, or measurement changes.
An observed model difference is a prior or aggregation artifact rather than component information.
Long-horizon disagreement is irreducible structural uncertainty, not a resolvable data deficit.

controls: frozen historical cutoff and holdout windows
identical posterior draw counts across compared models
mediators_or_moderators: education and contraception indicators where legally available

data_plan.core_source: WPP 2024 country-age-sex demographic series after license and release-version review.
data_plan.supplemental_sources: Pre-registered climate-disruption and contextual datasets only after provenance, spatial resolution, and license review.
data_plan.time_split: Rolling-origin historical training and held-out forecast windows; exact cutoffs are frozen before execution.
data_plan.missing_data: Do not silently impute. Record missingness by variable-country-year; use pre-specified model-based treatment only within sensitivity analyses and compare against complete-case-calibrated subsets.

comparators_and_ablations: deterministic cohort-component baseline with common central inputs
probabilistic ensemble with climate-disruption feature set
fertility-only, mortality-only, and migration-only counterfactual component swaps
country-level fit followed by independent region/world aggregation
alternative prior and historical-cutoff sensitivity runs

calibration_and_statistics.decision_rule: Call post-2100 persistence supported only if the selected model is not worse than the demographic baseline on pre-specified held-out metrics, has acceptable calibration, and its posterior probability of positive global growth at 2100 exceeds a threshold fixed before execution.
calibration_and_statistics.uncertainty: Report posterior intervals, between-model dispersion, and sensitivity to structural assumptions separately.
calibration_and_statistics.multiplicity: Treat country and component diagnostics as hierarchical estimates; do not interpret an unadjusted collection of country-level feature coefficients as confirmed effects.

replication_and_reproducibility.replication_unit: independent rolling-origin forecast origins and independently seeded posterior chains
replication_and_reproducibility.minimum_rationale: The number of forecast origins and posterior draws is selected by convergence, effective sample size, Monte Carlo error, and stability of decision outputs, not by a participant sample-size calculation.
replication_and_reproducibility.randomization_or_blinding: Not applicable to historical demographic records. Analysis code will hold out future observations by pre-declared time windows; model labels may be masked for a final score comparison when practical.
replication_and_reproducibility.software_provenance: Version-lock code, input files, configuration, random seeds, and output schema.

safety_ethics_governance.human_subjects: No human-subject recruitment or intervention is proposed.
safety_ethics_governance.privacy: Use aggregated public demographic data; do not merge personally identifying migration records.
safety_ethics_governance.harm_risk: Population scenarios can be misused to justify coercive reproductive or migration policy. Results must not be translated into individual, ethnic, national, or reproductive prescriptions.

falsification_criteria: Held-out calibration is materially below the pre-registered acceptance band.
The demographic-only baseline matches or exceeds the climate-feature model on primary scores.
A claimed persistence branch disappears under reasonable prior, input-vintage, or aggregation sensitivity checks.
Component swaps cannot identify a stable contribution to peak timing.
